title: Revisiting Fine-Tuning Strategies for Self-supervised Medical Imaging Analysis
mechanism: Fine-tuning intermediate layers is better than end-to-end; fine-tuning the first 75% of a network beats end-to-end by up to 5.48%.
adaptation: Freeze layer4 at its pretrained weights and train the rest; reuse when MIM / DDeP or domain SSL encoders are re-tried.
evidence: Four medical downstream tasks, several fine-tuning set sizes; up to +5.48% over end-to-end.
min_experiment: Arm layer4-frozen vs PF on 5-fold CV, 2 seeds. Kill if CV inactive IoU and relF1@2 not above PF.
prior_overlap: none for permanent block freezing; MIM / DDeP + PF n.d. used full-encoder tuning.
